title: Survey-date heat gave no clear next-year coral cover link in four Atlantic and Pacific samples in 2003-2018
abstract: We tested whether survey-date heat stress was linked to next-year hard-coral cover change in Reef Check records matched by site, calendar month and depth band. Four Atlantic and Pacific period models used 1,389 complete pairs in 2003-2018, with follow-up through 2019. Slopes ranged from -2.35 to +2.19 cover percentage points per four TSA degree-heating weeks. All four corrected intervals included zero. Only 45 pairs had heat of at least four. Usable follow-up covered 15.9% of 8,743 eligible baseline cells. Exact full-frame slope ranges with missing next-year cover from 0 to 100% permit both signs in all four samples. The archive did not establish a repeated link to additional later loss. This does not show that heat causes no harm. Baseline heat can miss later events, baseline cover can already reflect damage, and selective visits limit inference. The package gives source hashes, cells, code, endpoint assignments, model checks and a figure. It does not test species loss or air pollution.

display.caption: Complete-case heat slopes and exact missing-follow-up outcome ranges. Regional intervals on the left account for four tests. The right panel uses the full eligible frame and omits depth change. Its ranges are not confidence intervals.

citations.reason: We adapt its raw cell construction and matching code under the SCI baseline MIT terms. The new analysis tests heat as the exposure without requiring bleaching values and adds exact missing-follow-up bounds. Raw observations overlap.
